observations.fact: The outer loop copies/uploads all512 expert blobs once for a layer, checks the drain, then publishes the temporary full residency map before run_impl walks that layer in operator chunks.
observations.consequence: Increasing a MoE-only window does not itself reduce this path's host-to-device expert-weight byte volume. It must not be credited with the original chunk-major streaming transfer reduction.

observations.fact: The native FP16 expert branch dequantizes GU and down to the two-slot scratch pair inside compute(j,blob,...), then issues GU/activation/down using current expert ne. This occurs again when the next operator chunk reaches the same expert.
observations.consequence: A cross-chunk MoE window targets repeated VRAM dequantization, launch count, weight reuse and GEMM row shape; these are different resources from PCIe uploads.

observations.fact: Grouping builds per-chunk offsets and source/slot maps, then expert-ID order; combine consumes BF16 Dm and routing slots before the FFN HC write.
observations.consequence: A loop swap must retain inputs/intermediate HC state and defer final callbacks. Keeping current top-k output order can require substantial BF16 Dm storage; an FP32 accumulator changes summation order and needs a prospective numerical contract.

observations.fact: The current vLLM adapter selects compact16x64 for ne<128 and wide128x128 otherwise.
observations.consequence: The pending exact ne census can quantify grid/padding work, but not realized matrix utilization or speed. More rows are not automatically faster.

decision: R966 investigates a bounded16K MoE window while keeping GDN/QSA causal chunks at8K. No loop reorder, chunk-guard widening or new native/GPU execution was made. Current paired profile and source feasibility must inform the implementation choice.
separate_pcie_opportunity: Current all-GPU residual placement can remove host residual payload for the rows moved to VRAM; it is a separate prepared experiment with its own larger-context admission and matched timing gates.
